title: Florida turns Hurricane Ian pier wreckage into 300-ton underwater reef
content: In an inspiring move, pieces from the historical Naples Pier, damaged by Hurricane Ian, are being transformed into vital marine habitats. This initiative involves placing 59 concrete pilings at Wasmer Reef, providing support for diverse marine life. Not only does this project recycle construction debris, but it also fosters new ecosystems. Future reconstruction efforts for Naples Pier will emphasize improved safety and resilience to withstand upcoming storms.

title: Sara Blakely put $5,000 into Spanx; 21 years later, it was valued at $1.2bn
content: Sara Blakely founded Spanx in 2000 with $5,000 in savings while working as a door-to-door fax machine salesperson. Despite having no formal business training or outside investment, she built the company into a global womenswear brand. In 2021, Blackstone acquired a majority stake in the company at a $1.2 billion valuation, with Oprah Winfrey and Reese Witherspoon joining as investors.

title: US biotech firm completes 95% of dodo genome, targets bird’s possible revival
content: Colossal Biosciences aims to resurrect the extinct dodo bird using cutting-edge gene-editing technologies. By leveraging their sophisticated AI platform, GenoMorph, the company has pinpointed essential genetic traits. With 95% of the dodo genome analysis complete, their ambitious project is on track, though a specific timeline for the living dodo remains undisclosed. This groundbreaking venture is part of a larger initiative to counteract the effects of human-induced species extinction.

title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella responds to Virat Kohli's first-ever LinkedIn post

title: Texas judge overturns reservoir permit that could flood over 16,000 ranch acres

Wichita Falls aims to appeal this ruling as they push for their water supply plans. This situation underscores the complex relationship between infrastructure advancements and conservation, with the city's next moves remaining unclear.

title: Rare Nanotyrannus skeleton found on Montana ranch could fetch up to $9 million

This well-preserved specimen is anticipated to garner between $6 million and $9 million, creating a buzz among paleontologists and collectors alike due to its invaluable significance.

title: America’s fastest ocean liner to be sunk and turned into world’s largest reef

This initiative follows successful environmental remediation and requires final approvals. To honor its legacy, a visitor center will be established, promoting tourism and attracting divers and anglers eager to explore this underwater attraction.

title: Scientists recreate lost 1960s bird song; modern sparrows begin copying it
content: A groundbreaking approach has emerged, leveraging computer-generated recordings to rejuvenate the bird songs that nature has lost. Researchers successfully reintroduced the unique call of the rufous-collared sparrow back into its habitat in Argentina. This innovative conservation strategy seeks to bolster endangered species by preserving their vocal heritage and fostering communication skills, as demonstrated by positive outcomes in captive breeding for species such as the regent honeyeater.

title: WHO says childhood obesity needs more than medicine: What Indian families can do
content: Childhood obesity has become a pressing issue, necessitating a well-rounded strategy that promotes better nutrition and active lifestyles. According to the World Health Organization, minimizing screen time and ensuring adequate sleep are critical steps. Parents are encouraged to move away from using food as a reward and instead foster outdoor play. Building a family environment that supports healthy choices is vital, highlighting the importance of lifestyle changes over medical solutions.

title: Can a medical age certificate override school records for a govt job? HC answers

title: SC upholds HC order denying OBC reservation benefits to Hindu converts to Islam
content:
Converts to Islam from Hinduism cannot claim OBC reservation, rules Supreme Court

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday upheld a Madras high court ruling that a person who converts to Islam from Hinduism cannot claim reservation benefits under the Backward Class (BC) category. A bench of Justices PK Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar observed that a person who moves from the Hindu social order to a non-Hindu social order cannot claim such benefits. The Tamil Nadu government had challenged the Madras high court order before the Supreme Court. The high court had quashed the state government’s decision to recognise seven Muslim sects as Backward Classes, a move that allowed people from Hindu Backward Classes to be treated as Backward Class Muslims after converting to Islam.
